1.q: When all the work that Solomon did for the house of Yahweh was completed, Solomon brought
1.note: The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [When Solomon’s workers completed all of the work for the house of Yahweh, they brought] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))
storerooms, rooms where things are kept or stored

2.note: Alternate translation: [called together the leaders of Israel]

2.q: all the heads of the tribes
2.note: Here “heads” is a metaphor for the most important part of something. Alternate translation: [all the leaders of the tribes]

3.note: This may refer either: (1) to the people whom Solomon called to Jerusalem and who are listed in 5:2 or (2) generally to those who traveled to Jerusalem for the feast, not necessarily to every male person who lived in Israel.

3.q: at the feast, which was in the seventh month
3.note: This is the Festival of Shelters which is on the fifteenth day of the seventh month of the Hebrew calendar. This is near the beginning of October on Western calendars. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal); and [Assumed Knowledge and Implicit Information](ta:figs-explicit))

5.note: This refers to all of the bowls and tools that were used in the house of God. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 4:19

6.note: Here “all” is a generalization meaning very many Israelites.

6.q: sacrificing sheep and oxen that could not be counted
6.note: This is an exaggeration that emphasizes the great number of animals that were sacrificed. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [sacrificing more sheep and oxen than anyone could count] or [sacrificing very many sheep and oxen] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

7.q: into the inner room of the house, to the most holy place, under
7.note: Alternate translation: [into the inner room of the house—that is, to the most holy place—under]

8.q: poles by which it was carried
8.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [poles by which the priests carried it]

9.q: their ends were seen … they could not be seen
9.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people could see their ends … people could not see them]
This means the day on which the writer wrote.

11.note: This phrase is used here to mark an important event in the story. If your language has a way of doing this, you could consider using it here.

12.note: two thin, round metal plates that are hit together to make a loud sound

13.q: making one sound to be heard for praising and thanking Yahweh
13.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [making one sound as they praised and thanked Yahweh]
This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [sang loudly]

13.q: for his covenant loyalty endures forever
13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **covenant loyalty**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form such as “faithful.” Alternate translation: [for he is faithful forever]

13.q: Then the house, the house of Yahweh, was filled with a cloud
13.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Then a cloud filled the house of Yahweh]
